reason: Pharaoh, the primary elite figure in this passage, is portrayed unfavorably through his fear-driven paranoia ('a new king...who knew not Joseph'), cruel oppression of the Israelites (enslaving them with harsh labor), and murderous commands to kill Hebrew infants. His motivations are presented as selfish and morally reprehensible. While Pharaoh's daughter demonstrates compassion toward the infant Moses (showing mercy when she finds him), the dominant portrayal of the ruling elite is decidedly negative, emphasizing their tyranny and injustice.
